s: John, based at Gazara, is Simon's son who reported Cendebaeus's actions, led the army with Judas, and pursued the enemy, burning Azotus's towers. Warned after Ptolemy murdered his father, he killed the assassins sent for him, then succeeded Simon as high priest.

l: Simon, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Simon is a Jewish leader, son of Mattathias and brother of Judas and Jonathan, of the sons of Joarib. He is described as a man of counsel and father to his brothers, and he fought for Israel with his family since youth. The records follow him from soldier to ruler of his people and then to his death. Early on, Judas sends him with three thousand men to rescue the Jews of Galilee. He defeats the Gentiles, pursues them to the gate of Ptolemais, and brings the Galilean and Arbatta Jews to Judea. After Judas dies he helps bury him at Modin and flees with Jonathan to the wilderness of Tekoah. He joins an ambush of the children of Jambri, and at Bethbasi he burns Bacchides's siege engines and helps defeat him. He later supports Jonathan against Apollonius and at Azotus brings the army forward to defeat the phalanx. He takes Joppa and garrisons it, and builds Adida in the plain. When Jonathan falls, Simon encourages the fearful people and is accepted as leader in place of Judas and Jonathan. He pays Tryphon's ransom demand without result, buries Jonathan at Modin, and builds a tomb monument for his father, mother and four brothers. He fortifies Judea and secures peace and tax release from Demetrius, who confirms him as high priest and makes him a friend. He takes Gazara, Bethsura and the Jerusalem citadel, makes Joppa a harbor, and enlarges the borders. He glorifies the sanctuary, renews the alliance with Rome and Sparta, and sends Numenius to Rome with a gold shield. Contracts are dated by the first year of Simon. The people honor him as leader, governor and high priest, a position held until a faithful prophet arises, and his son John is made leader of all his forces. He answers Antiochus's demands by calling the lands his fathers' inheritance and offering one hundred talents for Joppa and Gazara. Now old, he sends his oldest sons Judas and John to fight in his place. On a visit to Jericho with his sons Mattathias and Judas in the 177th year, Ptolemy receives him deceitfully at Dok, and Simon is killed at a banquet.

l: Judas, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Judas, surnamed Maccabaeus, is a son of Mattathias, one of five brothers (including Simon and Jonathan), described as strong and mighty from his youth. Mattathias appoints him captain to fight the people's battle. He rises in his father's place, likened to a lion, hunting the lawless and turning wrath from Israel. The records portray him as a deliverer of Israel, renowned to the utmost part of the earth, with a memory blessed forever. Early on he kills Apollonius and keeps his sword, using it all his days, and routs Seron at Bethhoron. At Mizpeh and Emmaus he appoints captains of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, sends home those exempted by the law, and trusts heaven to save by many or by few. He defeats Gorgias' force at Emmaus, prays before meeting Lysias at Bethsura with ten thousand men, leads the cleansing of the holy place, and fortifies Mount Zion and Bethsura. He then defeats the children of Esau, Baean and the Ammonites, and leads eight thousand men with Jonathan into Gilead, taking cities, routing Timotheus, and bringing the Jews safely to Mount Zion. Glorified among Israel and the Gentiles, he strikes Hebron and Azotus, then besieges the citadel garrison in the 150th year. Accused to the king, he distrusts Bacchides, avoids Nicanor's deceit, and defeats Nicanor at Adasa on the thirteenth of Adar. He sends Eupolemus and Jason to Rome to seek friendship and alliance and freedom from the Greek yoke. At Elasa his three thousand chosen men dwindle to about eight hundred. Refusing to flee, he defeats Bacchides's right wing and pursues it to mount Azotus, but falls in battle. He is buried at Modin in his ancestors' tomb and mourned as the savior of Israel, his many other deeds left unwritten.

l: Eleazar, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_surname Avaran Eleazar, called Avaran, sees the tallest elephant in royal armor and thinks the king is on it. He charges through the phalanx, kills many, crawls under the elephant and kills it, and dies when it falls on him, giving his life for his people and an everlasting name.

l: Jonathan, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Jonathan is a man who rises from prince and leader of the Jews to high priest, governor and chief friend of the king, and who dies as a captive. He is chosen by the friends of Judas after Judas's death. He flees Bacchides, avenges his brother John, fortifies Bethbasi, then makes peace, settles at Michmash and judges the people, destroying the ungodly. Courted by rival kings, he accepts Alexander's appointment as high priest, wears the holy garments, and rebuilds Jerusalem's walls and Mount Zion. He captures Joppa, wins at Azotus, burns Dagon's temple, and receives Ekron and a gold buckle. Demetrius and later Antiochus confirm his priesthood and grant exemptions, golden vessels and purple clothing. He besieges the Jerusalem citadel, takes Gaza's hostages, and at Hazor turns a fleeing army into a rout after tearing his clothes and praying. He seeks friendship with Rome and claims kinship with the Spartans. He strengthens Jerusalem's walls and isolates the citadel. Trusting Tryphon at Bethshan, he goes to Ptolemais with a thousand men and is seized there. Tryphon holds him on a claim of debt, then kills him near Bascama after being paid. Israel mourns. His brother Simon later moves his bones to Modin and buries him there.

l: Modin, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Modin is the city of Simon's fathers, with an altar. Mattathias lives there, kills a Jew and the king's officer enforcing sacrifice, tears down the altar, and is buried there. Later Simon buries Jonathan's bones and builds a lasting family tomb.

l: king's officers, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_role enforcers of the apostasy The king's officers enforce the apostasy and come to Modin to compel sacrifice, offering Mattathias honors of silver, gold and the status of the king's friends. After he refuses, one officer is killed by Mattathias, and others pursue the refugees into the wilderness and attack them on the Sabbath.

l: king (the ruler over the Jews), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: The king issues a commandment requiring sacrifice and abandonment of ancestral worship, which all the nations and many in Judah have followed. Mattathias refuses to heed his words, and his officers promise rewards for compliance and pursue those who break his command.

l: covenant of the fathers, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: is_a commandment of the fathers [to be kept by Israel faithfully] Mattathias vows that he, his sons and kindred will walk in the covenant of their fathers and not forsake the law and ordinances. He calls those zealous for the law to follow him, and his army rescues the law from the Gentiles and kings; he charges his sons to give their lives for the covenant.

l: Sabbath, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: The Sabbath is a day not to be profaned; refugees who refused to fight on it were attacked and about a thousand died, so Mattathias and his friends decided fighting in defense is permitted.

l: Jewish refugees in the wilderness, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Justice-seeking refugees flee multiplied evils into the wilderness with families and livestock; the king's forces overtake them on the Sabbath, and they refuse to fight, about a thousand dying while proclaiming innocence.

l: Hasidaeans, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: The Hasidaeans were a company of mighty men of Israel devoted to the law who joined Mattathias's uprising. They were first to seek peace with Alcimus and Bacchides, trusting his oath, but sixty were killed in one day, spreading fear among the people.

l: Mattathias's uprising, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Mattathias leads an uprising to rescue the law from the Gentiles: after killing an apostate and the king's officer at Modin, he and his sons flee, resolve to fight on the Sabbath, gather allies, strike sinners, pull down altars, and prosper.

l: Apollonius, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: governs Coelesyria Appointed by the younger Demetrius over Coelesyria, Apollonius camped at Jamnia and sent Jonathan a taunting challenge to fight in the plain. He lost Joppa to Jonathan, then used cavalry and a hidden ambush of a thousand horsemen at Azotus, but his forces were exhausted and defeated.

l: Seron, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Seron is a Syrian army commander who seeks fame by fighting Judas and those defying the king's command; he marches a mighty ungodly army to Bethhoron's ascent, where Judas Maccabaeus defeats him.

l: Lysias, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Lysias is an honorable man of royal lineage, left by King Antiochus to govern royal affairs from the Euphrates to Egypt's borders and to guard the king's son Antiochus. Given half the forces and the elephants, he is charged to root out Israel and settle foreigners on its land. He sends Ptolemy, Nicanor, and Gorgias against Judah, but they are defeated. Discouraged, he gathers sixty thousand infantry and five thousand cavalry the next year, is defeated at Bethsura, and withdraws to Antioch to hire more soldiers. After the old king's death he installs the son as king. When Philip returns, Lysias persuades the king and leaders to make peace with the Jews and restore their laws, citing weakness and scant food.

l: Nicanor, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Nicanor, an arrogant prince of the king who hated Israel, came to Jerusalem with a great army to destroy its people. He tried deceiving Judas with false peace, lost about five hundred men, mocked priests and swore to burn the temple, then fell first at Adasa; his head and hand were hung.

l: Gorgias, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: commands Gorgias' army [took five thousand infantry and a thousand chosen cavalry] Gorgias takes five thousand infantry and a thousand cavalry on a night march, guided by the men of the citadel, to surprise the Jews. He finds Judas' camp empty and searches the mountains, believing the Jews are fleeing, then sees the burning camp and his army flees.

l: Judas's kindred and followers, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: supports Judas Maccabaeus [fought with gladness] Judas's kindred and his father's supporters help him and fight gladly for Israel. At Bethhoron his small, hungry company fears Seron's army but is encouraged by Judas and wins. At Mizpeh they fast and pray, and then are organized into captains of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, with some sent home according to the law.

l: lawless and ungodly men of Israel, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: is_appointed_by Bacchides [made rulers of the country] After Judas died the lawless emerged throughout Israel, and Bacchides made the ungodly rulers of the country. They searched out Judas's friends for vengeance, later counseled Bacchides against Jonathan, and were angrily killed in large numbers when his plan failed, with about fifty slain by Jonathan's men.

l: Syrian army, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_size forty thousand infantry and seven thousand cavalry [sent by Lysias against Judah] Syrian forces under Seron are defeated at Bethhoron, with about eight hundred killed and the rest fleeing to the land of the Philistines. A far larger force of forty thousand infantry and seven thousand cavalry, led by Ptolemy, Nicanor, and Gorgias, then camps near Emmaus. Forces of Syria and of the Philistines join merchants who come to buy captives.

l: Judea, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Judea is a land contested and defended across the records. First guarded by Joseph and Azarias, it shelters rescued Jews and marks the pursuit's limit. Jonathan then secures tribute freedom and expanded territory from Demetrius. Finally Antiochus blames Simon for harm there, Simon calls it the fathers' inheritance, and Cendebaeus invades, killing and raiding.

l: Antioch, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Ptolemy entered Antioch and put on the crown of Asia. Later its people, numbering 120,000, rose to kill Demetrius, but the Jews sent by Jonathan killed about 100,000, set the city on fire and forced peace. Tryphon afterward took control of the city.

l: Emmaus, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_terrain plain country Emmaus, in the plain country, is where the Syrian army under Ptolemy, Nicanor, and Gorgias encamps. Merchants and allied forces gather there, and Judas's army later camps on its south side.

l: God, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: God, also called heaven, is portrayed as redeemer and Savior of Israel who grants victory in battle, since strength comes from heaven rather than from army size. Judas trusts him to crush the enemy, and the people cry out to him at Mizpeh. Later Judas invokes the covenant, recalling the Red Sea and David, and the people thank him as good, whose mercy endures forever.

l: Battle of Bethhoron, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_outcome Seron's army defeated, about eight hundred fell Seron's large army meets Judas's small company at the ascent of Bethhoron. After Judas's speech, he rushes suddenly against them and they are defeated. They are pursued down the descent to the plain, about eight hundred fall, and the rest flee to Philistine land, spreading fear of Judas among the nations.

l: fasting and prayer at Mizpeh, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: takes_place_at Mizpeh [traditional place of prayer for Israel] The Israelites gather at Mizpeh, a former place of prayer for Israel, and fast, wear sackcloth, put ashes on their heads, and tear their clothes. They open the book of the law, bring priestly garments, first fruits, and tithes, and stir up the Nazarites. They cry to heaven for help against the assembled Gentiles, then sound trumpets and shout.

l: Gorgias' army, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_guides men of the citadel [guides for night march] Gorgias' army moves out at night, finds the Jewish camp empty, and is scattered. Those in the rear fall by the sword, about three thousand are killed, and the survivors on the mountain, seeing the smoke of the burning camp, flee into the land of the Philistines.

l: Jews (Judas's followers), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Judas's followers are a Jewish army opposed by ungodly men of Israel. Though only three thousand and lacking desired armor and swords, they sound trumpets, rout the Gentile force, plunder its camp, and give thanks. Ten thousand later defeat Lysias' army at Bethsura, and they cleanse the temple. They fortify the sanctuary and Bethsura and burn the king's engines, but famine weakens them and the king's broken oath deceives them.

l: Gentiles, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_camp_quality strong and fortified [camp surrounded by cavalry expert in war] The Gentile forces are defeated at Emmaus, and Judas hopes all the Gentiles will know that one redeems Israel. They had profaned the sanctuary and altar, and the reproach of the Gentiles is turned away at the rededication. Judas fortifies Zion so they cannot trample it again.

l: Lysias' army (Lysias), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: encamps_at Bethsura Lysias' army of sixty thousand chosen infantry and five thousand cavalry encamps at Bethsura in Idumaea. About five thousand of its men fall in battle against Judas' men, and the rest are put to flight.

l: people of the citadel (Jerusalem citadel garrison), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: is_located_in citadel (Jerusalem's citadel) [starved under blockade] The people of the citadel ask Tryphon to come through the wilderness and send them food, but snow stops him. Cut off from the country and from trade, many die of famine, and they beg Simon for his right hand. He gives it but expels them from the citadel.

l: Gazara, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Gazara is a city on the borders of Azotus. Simon besieges it with a siege engine, captures a tower, expels the people, cleanses idol houses, settles law-keeping men, fortifies it, and builds a dwelling; his son John later leads forces there. Antiochus demands it back; Simon cites its harm and offers one hundred talents with Joppa.

l: Azotus, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_temple Dagon [Beth-dagon, burned by Jonathan] Apollonius went to Azotus and the armies joined battle there. After his cavalry was defeated, survivors fled into Beth-dagon, and Jonathan burned Azotus, the nearby cities, and the temple of Dagon with those inside.

l: Bethsura, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Bethsura is a city on Judea's borders, fortified by the Jews; the king's army attacks, its people make peace and leave for lack of Sabbath-year food, and the king garrisons it.

l: Mount Zion, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Mount Zion is a sanctuary site found desolate when Judas's army arrives; its holy place is cleansed while men fight the citadel, then it is fortified with high walls and towers, garrisoned by Judas.

l: altar of burnt offerings, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: The altar of burnt offerings, found defiled by the Gentiles, is pulled down by deliberating priests to avoid reproach; its stones are stored on the temple hill until a prophet answers.

l: new altar, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: A new altar built of whole stones according to the law, like the former one. It was dedicated on the twenty-fifth of Chislev, the day the Gentiles profaned the old altar, with sacrifice and music lasting eight days.

l: cleansing and rededication of the temple, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Cleansing and rededication of the temple: after victories, Judas and kindred resolve to purify the desecrated holy place; blameless priests cleanse it, make a new altar and vessels, burn incense, light lamps, set loaves, then celebrate eight days, annually.

l: battle at Emmaus, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Battle at Emmaus: after Gorgias' night march finds Judas' camp empty, Judas' three thousand strike at daybreak, defeat the Gentiles, pursue them to several cities, kill about three thousand, burn the camp, and send survivors fleeing to Philistia.

l: battle at Bethsura, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_casualties about five thousand [of Lysias' army] The following year Lysias encamps at Bethsura in Idumaea with a large army and Judas meets him with ten thousand men after a prayer for help. About five thousand of Lysias' men fall, and Lysias withdraws to Antioch to gather hired soldiers.

l: Joseph the son of Zacharias, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: is_a leader of the people [left to guard Judea] Joseph is left with Azarias as a leader of the people in Judea, with orders from Judas to fight no battle with the Gentiles until Judas returns. Hearing of the others' exploits, he wants to get a name for himself and marches toward Jamnia, where he is put to flight and pursued to the borders of Judea.

l: Azarias, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: is_a leader of the people [left to guard Judea] Azarias is left with Joseph to lead the people and guard Judea, and is told not to fight the Gentiles until Judas returns. He joins Joseph in seeking a name, attacks at Jamnia, and is routed by Gorgias. The text says they were not of the family of those by whom deliverance was given to Israel.

l: Timotheus, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: is_a leader of the Ammonite army [also leader of the Gentile army against Gilead] Timotheus leads the Ammonite forces defeated by Judas and later commands the Gentile army besieging the strongholds in Gilead. His army flees from Judas with about eight thousand dead, and he gathers another army near Raphon, where he says Judas will defeat them if he crosses first. Judas does cross first and defeats them.

l: Judas's army, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Judas's army of eight thousand goes with him to Gilead, fights in three companies with trumpets and prayer, and captures several cities. It pursues Ephron's conquest, escorts the Gilead Jews home, and returns with not one man slain.

l: Gilead, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Gilead is the land where Jews are besieged in Bosora, Bosor, Alema, Casphor, Maked, Carnaim, and other cities, and where they flee to the stronghold of Dathema. Judas conquers Bosora, Mizpeh, Casphor, Maked, Bosor, and other cities there, then removes the Jews to Judah.

l: Galilee, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: is_a land of the Gentiles [called Galilee of the Gentiles] Messengers from Galilee report that people of Ptolemais, Tyre, Sidon, and all Galilee of the Gentiles have gathered to destroy the Jews there. Simon goes in, defeats the Gentiles, and brings the Jews of Galilee and Arbatta to Judea.

l: Ptolemais, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Ptolemais is a city contested among rulers: Demetrius offered it to the Jerusalem sanctuary, Alexander took it, wed Cleopatra and honored Jonathan there, but Tryphon's promise of it to Jonathan ended with gates shut and Jonathan seized.

l: Ephron, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_attribute large and very strong [city on the road to Judah] Ephron is a large, strong city on the road home from Gilead that the army must pass through. Its people block the gates with stones and refuse Judas's peaceful offer of passage. Judas fights it a day and a night, takes it, kills all the males, razes it, and passes through over the slain.

l: Judas's campaign in Gilead, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_outcome all Israelites in Gilead brought safely to Judea [none slain on return] Judas and Jonathan cross the Jordan after letters report the Gentile threat and learn from the Nabathaeans of the sieges. They capture Bosora, rout Timotheus, take Mizpeh and other cities, destroy Carnaim, take Ephron, and lead the Jews of Gilead home to Judah with no losses.

l: Defeat of Joseph and Azarias at Jamnia, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Joseph and Azarias, disobeying Judas's order, march on Jamnia seeking renown; Gorgias meets them, routs them, and pursues them to Judea's borders, killing about two thousand Israelites, a defeat blamed on ignoring Judas.

l: Antiochus his son (Eupator), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Antiochus Eupator, raised by Lysias, is set up as king after his father's death. He marches against Judas with a large army, makes peace on Lysias's counsel, breaks the oath, returns to Antioch, and seizes it from Philip.

l: Philip (friend of Antiochus), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Philip, a friend of the king, is appointed by the dying Antiochus as guardian of his young son, receiving crown, robe and signet ring. He returns from Persia and Media with forces to seize government, holds Antioch, until the young king takes it by force.

l: king's army, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: The king's army, of 100,000 infantry, 20,000 cavalry, 32 elephants and hired foreign soldiers, advances splendidly to Bethzacharias, loses 600 men in the first clash, takes Bethsura, and besieges the sanctuary until peace.

l: elephants (king's war elephants), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Thirty-two king's war elephants, each carrying a wooden tower with four men and an Indian driver and escorted by 1,000 infantry and 500 cavalry, are given grape and mulberry juice, distributed among phalanxes; the tallest is killed by Eleazar and falls on him.

l: siege of Jerusalem citadel, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Judas besieges the citadel in the 150th year using mounds and war engines; escaped besieged men and ungodly Israelites appeal to the king, provoking his campaign.

l: battle at Bethzacharias, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: is_located_at Bethzacharias [Judas encamped near the king's camp] The king's huge army, with elephants, glittering shields, and trumpets, meets Judas at Bethzacharias, and 600 of the king's men fall. Eleazar kills an elephant and dies, and the Jews turn away from the army's strength.

l: peace treaty and its breaking, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: A peace treaty proposed by Lysias lets the Jews keep their laws; the king and princes swear to it and defenders leave the stronghold, but the king, seeing Mount Zion's strength, breaks his oath and orders the wall pulled down.

l: Demetrius, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Demetrius, son of Seleucus, is a king who comes out of Rome with few men to a coastal city and reigns there. He refuses to see Antiochus and Lysias, whom the army kills, and takes his throne. He sends Bacchides, Alcimus and Nicanor against Israel. Rival of Alexander Epiphanes, he gathers forces and offers Jonathan concessions, which are distrusted because of past evils. He dies in battle against Alexander.

l: Antiochus, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Antiochus is a name borne by kings in these records. One is Alexander's young child, raised by Imalcue, crowned under Tryphon, who confirms Jonathan's high priesthood and makes Simon governor. Another, son of Demetrius and called a great king of Asia, claims his fathers' kingdom, courts Simon with tax remissions and coinage rights, then rejects his help, cancels covenants, demands cities or money, and sends Cendebaeus against Judea while pursuing Tryphon. He also pays tribute to Romans.

l: Alcimus, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Alcimus is an ungodly man who sought the high priesthood and led lawless Israelites in accusing Judas to the king. Demetrius appointed him high priest and sent him with Bacchides. He swore peace to the Hasidaeans, yet sixty of them were killed. Struggling to keep his office, he returned to the king with evil accusations, prompting Nicanor's mission. Later he ordered the sanctuary's inner court wall pulled down, was struck with palsy, lost speech, and died in torment.

l: Bacchides, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Bacchides is a powerful, faithful friend of the king who ruled beyond the river, chosen by Demetrius to take vengeance on Israel. He first came with a great army, offered deceitful peace to Judas, camped at Bezeth, killed deserters and others in a pit, left Alcimus in charge, and returned to the king. Sent again with Alcimus, he fought Judas at Elasa, installed ungodly rulers, hunted Judas's friends, pursued Jonathan, fortified Bethsura and Gazara, and held hostages in Jerusalem. After defeat at Bethbasi, he swore peace with Jonathan, returned captives, and never re-entered Judah.

l: Battle at Adasa, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Judas camped at Adasa with three thousand men and prayed for God to crush the enemy. On the thirteenth of Adar the armies met; Nicanor fell first, his army fled, and pursuers to Gazara, aided by villagers, killed them all.

l: Day of Nicanor (festival), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Day of Nicanor is a festival of great gladness, ordained by the Jews after their victory to be kept yearly on the thirteenth of Adar; afterward Judah had rest briefly.

l: Romans, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: The Romans are portrayed as valiant men who befriend those who rely on them and destroy opponents. They conquered the Gauls, defeated Philip and Perseus, and captured Antiochus alive, giving his lands to Eumenes. They hold the Greeks in bondage and can make and depose kings, yet none wears a crown or purple. A 320-man senate and one yearly ruler govern them. They welcome the Jewish embassy, agree to an alliance, and warn Demetrius.

l: Eupolemus, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_father John Eupolemus, son of John, son of Accos, is chosen by Judas as an envoy. He travels with Jason on the long journey to Rome and speaks before the senate to request an alliance.

l: Jason, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_father Eleazar Jason, son of Eleazar, is chosen by Judas to go to Rome with Eupolemus. He helps present the Jewish request for alliance and friendship to the senate.

l: Jews, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: The Jews are a people regarded by the Gentiles as a state without a ruler, yet permitted by Antiochus to coin their own money. Their story centers on shifting alliances with powerful kings and a lasting friendship with Rome. Under Judas they seek Roman friendship to escape Greek bondage, and Rome registers them as allies and pledges defense against Demetrius. They reject Demetrius's offers, remembering his evil, and side with Alexander. Later Demetrius grants exemptions; three thousand Jewish men save him in Antioch, but he breaks faith. After Jonathan's capture they mourn, fearing neighboring Gentiles who seek their destruction. Jonathan's embassies renew ties with Sparta and Rome. Under Simon, Jews garrison key towns and accept him as leader and high priest. Antiochus confirms tax remissions and coinage, and Rome warns kings not to harm them, though Cendebaeus still raids Judea.

l: Roman alliance treaty, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: A treaty of alliance between the Romans and the Jews, inscribed on bronze tables and sent to Jerusalem as a memorial of peace. Each side pledges willing military aid in war and withholds supplies, food, weapons, money, and ships from the other's enemies. Both may add or remove terms by mutual agreement, with changes ratified.

l: Roman conquests, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: includes Spain [to take control of its silver and gold mines] Judas is told of Roman victories over the Gauls, in Spain where they took the silver and gold mines, and over Philip, Perseus, and Antiochus, who was captured with his 120 elephants and made to pay tribute and give hostages and land. Other kingdoms and islands that rose against Rome were destroyed and made servants, while those far and near feared its fame.

l: children of Jambri, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: The children of Jambri came out of Medaba and seized John and all he had. Jonathan and Simon ambushed their wedding procession, killing many and taking the spoils, which turned the wedding into mourning and avenged the blood of their brother.

l: Judas's army, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Judas's army of three thousand chosen men at Elasa, terrified by enemy numbers, shrank to eight hundred; those remaining fought all day and beat the right wing, but fled when Judas fell.

l: Bacchides's army, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_size twenty thousand infantry and two thousand cavalry Bacchides's army had twenty thousand infantry and two thousand cavalry. Its right wing was defeated by Judas, but its left wing followed and the battle turned desperate. Later about a thousand of its men fell at the Jordan, and it was defeated at Bethbasi, where its engines were burned.

l: battle at Elasa, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: lasts morning until evening At Elasa, Judas's eight hundred men faced Bacchides's much larger army, and the fighting lasted from morning until evening. Judas routed the right wing and pursued it to mount Azotus, but the left wing followed him, many fell on both sides, and Judas was killed.

l: death of Judas, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: occurs_in battle at Elasa Judas fell at the desperate battle at Elasa and the rest fled. Jonathan and Simon buried him in his ancestors' tomb at Modin, and all Israel mourned many days, saying how the mighty had fallen.

l: peace treaty (Jonathan and Bacchides), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: requires captives [Bacchides restores them to Jonathan] After his defeat at Bethbasi, Bacchides decided to leave, and Jonathan sent ambassadors proposing peace and the return of captives. Bacchides accepted, swore never to seek Jonathan's harm, restored the captives from Judah, and departed without returning to their borders.

l: Alexander Epiphanes, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Alexander, son of Antiochus, takes Ptolemais in the 160th year and reigns there, appoints Jonathan high priest and friend, fights Demetrius, marries Ptolemy's daughter Cleopatra, honors Jonathan, then grieves and returns to Antioch.

l: Demetrius, son of Demetrius, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Demetrius, son of Demetrius, returned from Crete to his ancestral land in the 165th year; his arrival distressed Alexander, who went back to Antioch and appointed Apollonius over Coelesyria.

l: Joppa, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Joppa is a seaside harbor, entrance for the islands of the sea. It first shut out Jonathan, whose forces won it after fighting when the frightened people opened to him. Later Antiochus demanded it back from Simon, who said it harmed the people and offered a hundred talents.

l: Demetrius's letter and offers to the Jews, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Demetrius's letter offered the Jews relief from tributes, salt tax and crown levies, plus captives' release, Jerusalem's holiness, citadel control, territory, money and building costs; Jonathan and the people rejected everything, distrusting him over past evil in Israel.

l: high priesthood, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Alexander appointed Jonathan high priest of his nation and king's friend, sending a purple robe and golden crown. Jonathan put on the holy garments at the feast of tabernacles in the seventh month of the 160th year.

l: battle between Alexander and Demetrius, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Alexander gathered great forces and camped near Demetrius, and the two kings joined battle. Alexander's army fled and Demetrius pursued, but Demetrius fell that day as the battle continued until sunset. Alexander afterward claimed to have overthrown Demetrius and taken his throne.

l: battle at Azotus, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: has_outcome Jonathan's victory [Simon's phalanx defeated the exhausted cavalry] Apollonius's cavalry surrounded Jonathan's army and shot arrows from morning until evening, while the people stood fast and the horses tired. Simon then attacked and routed them, and Jonathan burned Azotus and Dagon's temple, with about eight thousand killed by sword or fire.

l: Demetrius, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Demetrius is a king who married Ptolemy's daughter and won Jonathan over with gifts and tax relief. After dismissing most troops, who hated him, he was saved by Jonathan's men, then lied and treated Jonathan harshly, and was finally routed by Tryphon and Antiochus and fled.

l: Tryphon, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Tryphon is an ambitious usurper, once a supporter of Alexander. He exploits discontent against Demetrius, routs him, and installs the young Antiochus as king, gaining the elephants and control of Antioch. Coveting rule over Asia, he moves against Antiochus and fears Jonathan, whom he deceives at Bethshan and seizes at Ptolemais. He invades Judah with a large army, demands money and hostages without releasing Jonathan, and, turned back by heavy snow, kills him near Bascama. He then deceitfully kills the young Antiochus, takes the crown of Asia, and brings calamity; Simon calls his deeds plunder. Finally, deserted by his forces, he flees to Dor, is besieged, and escapes by ship to Orthosia with Antiochus's forces pursuing.

l: people of Antioch, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: is_hostile_to Demetrius [wanted to kill the king] The people of Antioch gathered to the number of 120,000, wanted to kill Demetrius, and seized the main streets. The Jews killed about 100,000 of them and burned the city, and they then threw away their weapons, pleaded for the king's right hand, and made peace.

l: Demetrius' grants to the Jews, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Demetrius' permanent grants to the Jews: via a letter to Lasthenes he confirmed Judea's borders, added three governments, returned tithes, taxes, salt pits and crown taxes, ordered a copy displayed on the holy mountain, but later lied and treated Jonathan harshly.

l: Spartans, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: The Spartans are a people presented as kindred of the Jews, both said to descend from Abraham. Jonathan wrote to them, recalling King Arius's earlier letter to Onias. After Jonathan's death, they grieved and wrote on brass tablets to Simon, renewing friendship and alliance, honorably receiving ambassadors Numenius and Antipater.

l: Demetrius' princes, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Demetrius' princes returned with a larger army to fight Jonathan, and he met them at Hamath. Hearing that Jonathan's men were armed and ready, they feared, left fires burning in their camp, and withdrew across the river Eleutherus, where Jonathan failed to overtake them.

l: people of Ptolemais, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: inhabit Ptolemais The people of Ptolemais shut the gates when Jonathan entered, seized him, and killed with the sword all those who had come in with him.

l: Jonathan's army, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Jonathan came to Bethshan with forty thousand chosen men, then sent them home to Judah at Tryphon's request, keeping three thousand, of whom two thousand stayed in Galilee and one thousand went with him. The thousand were killed at Ptolemais, and the men in Galilee, learning of it, marched close together ready to fight, so their pursuers turned back and they reached Judah in peace.

l: alliance and friendship with Rome and Sparta, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Jonathan sent Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason to Rome to renew the former friendship and alliance, and told them to go also to the Spartans with his letters. Rome received them and gave letters for safe conduct, while the Spartan link rested on Arius's earlier letter claiming kinship. Rome and Sparta renewed with Simon the friendship and alliance confirmed with Judas and Jonathan, sending letters on brass tablets that were read at Jerusalem. The Spartan letter records the ambassadors Numenius and Antipater, and Simon sent Numenius to Rome with a gold shield to confirm the alliance.

l: King Demetrius, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: King Demetrius is a king who answers Simon's request with a friendly letter, accepting his golden crown and palm branch, confirming earlier grants and the strongholds Simon built, forgiving faults and the crown tax, releasing the Jews from tribute, and offering court enrollment and peace. He later goes into Media against Tryphon, is seized by Arsaces' forces, and is held captive under guard.

l: people of Judah (Simon's people), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: The people of Judah tremble at Tryphon's approach but revive when Simon speaks, and they promise to do all he tells them as their leader. Fear of their reaction leads Simon to send the ransom, and they mourn Jonathan many days. After the yoke is lifted they date contracts by the first year of Simon. Simon's nation tilled their land in peace, with the old men conversing in the streets and the young men in warlike apparel. They thanked Simon and his sons, proclaimed his deeds in a great congregation, made him leader and high priest, and consented to ordain that he act according to the decree.

l: tomb monument (Simon's tomb at Modin), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Simon's tomb at Modin is a high monument of polished stone, built with seven pyramids for his parents and four brothers, and adorned with pillars bearing armor and carved ships seen by sailors; it still stands.

l: hostages (Jonathan's money and sons demanded by Tryphon), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: consists_of one hundred talents of silver and two sons [demanded by Tryphon] Tryphon demands a hundred talents of silver and two of Jonathan's sons as hostages, claiming a debt to the king's treasury. Simon knows it is deceit but sends them so he will not be blamed for Jonathan's death. Tryphon takes the children and money but does not release Jonathan.

l: end of Gentile yoke (year 170), The First Book of the Maccabees
s: occurs_in year 170 [yoke taken away from Israel] In the 170th year, following Demetrius's letter releasing the Jews from tribute, the yoke of the Gentiles is taken from Israel. The people begin writing contracts dated 'the first year of Simon, the great high priest and captain and leader of the Jews.'

l: bronze tablets, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Bronze tablets honoring Simon: the Spartans first wrote to renew friendship, then the people inscribed his deeds and honors on brass tablets set on pillars on Mount Zion, ordering display in a conspicuous sanctuary place, with copies in the treasury for Simon and sons.

l: high priesthood, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: held_by Simon [leader and high priest forever, until a faithful prophet arises] Simon was made high priest in place of Jonathan, and the people made him leader and high priest for his faith and justice. The decree confirms the office as his forever until a faithful prophet arises, and Demetrius also confirmed it to him; Simon accepted it along with the roles of captain, governor and protector.

l: peace and prosperity under Simon, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: An era of rest in the land during all the days of Simon: people farm in peace, each sitting unafraid under vine and fig tree. Enemies are gone, kings defeated, cities supplied and defended, and Simon's fame reaches the earth's end.

l: Dor, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: located_by sea Dor, a city by the sea, is where Tryphon flees as his forces desert him. Antiochus encamps against it with 120,000 men and 8,000 cavalry, and ships join the attack so that no one can go in or out.

l: Athenobius, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Athenobius, a friend of Antiochus, is sent to demand Joppa, Gazara and the Jerusalem citadel from Simon, is amazed by Simon's glory, gets no answer to Simon's counter-offer, and returns enraged to the king.

l: Cendebaeus, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Cendebaeus is a military commander appointed chief captain of the sea coast by Antiochus, with infantry and cavalry, and ordered to fight Judea. He comes to Jamnia, invades, takes captives, kills people, and builds up Kidron for raids. John reports to Simon, and the Jewish army meets him across a brook; his forces are routed and flee to Kidron.

l: siege of Dor, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Antiochus besieges Dor by land and sea with 120,000 infantry, 8,000 cavalry, and ships, trapping Tryphon, who ultimately escapes by ship to Orthosia.

l: demand for cities or payment, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Antiochus, via Athenobius, demands Simon surrender Joppa, Gazara and the Jerusalem citadel with tributes, or pay one thousand talents of silver, or face attack. Simon refuses, citing ancestral inheritance, offers one hundred talents for Joppa and Gazara, and the king is enraged.

l: Roman letter of protection for the Jews, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: A letter from consul Lucius to King Ptolemy, brought by Numenius from Rome after Jewish ambassadors renewed friendship and gave a thousand-mina gold shield. It forbids kings to fight the Jews or aid their enemies, orders troublemakers handed to Simon, and was sent to many rulers.

l: Ptolemy, The First Book of the Maccabees
s: Ptolemy son of Abubus, wealthy governor of the plain of Jericho and the high priest's son-in-law, grows proud and plots to master the country. He deceitfully receives Simon and his sons at Dok and murders Simon and two sons at a banquet. He then seeks royal forces, targets John at Gazara, bribes captains, and sends men against Jerusalem; the text condemns this as great iniquity.
